question: Was the dismissal of Marc Dubois for serious cause on 16 March 2026 valid?
expected_answer: High risk that the dismissal is too late. The HR Director (competent to dismiss) received unambiguous DLP evidence on 06/03/2026; the Sales Director's e-mail of 09/03 shows the investigation was used to postpone the decision until after the Q1 closing for commercial reasons. An investigation/hearing only delays the 3-working-day period (art. 35 Law 1978) if it is genuinely needed and conducted promptly. Even if 13/03 were accepted as the knowledge date, seriousness is debatable (open VPN ticket, 9 years without warning, files deleted). The mailbox evidence was obtained without the CCT 81 procedure; it is probably still admissible (Antigone case law) but is not needed for the main facts. Expect exposure to an indemnity in lieu of notice (art. 39) and a possible CCT 109 claim; consider settlement.
key_facts: 05/03 18:12–18:19 CRM export + pricing file to personal Drive/Gmail (REC-Q01-01)
06/03 09:14 IT Security e-mails the evidence to HR Director and Sales Director (EML-Q01-01)
09/03 Sales Director: 'We know enough ... not before the Q1 closing on the 13th' (EML-Q01-03)
13/03 HR report claims certainty only after hearing (INV-Q01-01); dismissal 16/03 (LTR-Q01-01)
VPN incident open since 02/03 (REC-Q01-02, CHAT-Q01-01, STM-Q01-02)

sides.EML-Q01-01: evidence sent to the competent person on 06/03
sides.EML-Q01-03: decision deliberately delayed for business reasons

conflicts.resolution: Knowledge date most likely 06/03 (or at the latest 09/03); dismissal on 16/03 is late.
conflicts.why: Contemporaneous e-mails outweigh a self-serving report written by the dismissing party; the disciplinary policy itself forbids delaying for reasons unrelated to establishing facts.

conflicts.issue: Is the fact a serious cause?

sides.POL-WORKREG-2025-FR: lists transfer of confidential data to private storage as serious cause
sides.LAW-BE-1978-ART35-FR: serious cause is left to the judge's appreciation
sides.REC-Q01-02: documented VPN problem supports the explanation

conflicts.resolution: The list in the work regulations does not bind the judge; mitigating context is real.
conflicts.why: Mandatory law ranks above work regulations.

sides.INV-Q01-02: full mailbox searched without CCT 81 procedure

conflicts.resolution: Irregularly obtained; probably admissible under Antigone doctrine but weakens the employer.
conflicts.why: Generally binding CCT ranks above the IT policy.
